A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RandomWorld and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite layout changes and the relocation of GRPO training details from Appendix C to Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama and Qwen fine-tuning experiments, benchmark evaluations, and a tool/task-count scalability study in Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds a RandomWorld result for GPT-3.5, a manual information-leakage audit, and GRPO agent trajectories.

M1.justification: The type-guided tool and trajectory generation, environment caching, instruction verification, and SFT/GRPO procedures remain the same. Corrected illustrative type annotations and expanded documentation do not establish a changed algorithm or component.

E1.justification: Both versions use RandomWorld, ToolQA Easy/Hard, and NESTFUL with the same task and domain coverage. The new leakage audit samples existing RandomWorld training data; additional illustrative tools and trajectories do not establish expanded experimental coverage.

E2.justification: GPT-3.5 joins the RandomWorld comparison in Table 2, where v1 reported no score. It already participated in the ToolQA comparison. Other comparator memberships are unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces manual inspection of 200 randomly sampled training task/instruction pairs, flagging instruction substrings similar or identical to tool names or descriptions. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, training budgets, and testing procedures remain unchanged. Section 4.5's proposed early-stopping threshold is not reported as an implemented setting.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted information-leakage audit with examples and three Llama-RW-GRPO trajectories illustrating successful execution, recovery from formatting errors, and failure. The existing scalability ablation and five synthetic SFT examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new audit supplies a sample count and proportion but adds no uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds GPT-3.5's RandomWorld accuracy of 0.348; all other entries and all of Table 3 are unchanged. Appendix C newly reports potential leakage in 133/200 instructions (66.5%), with none judged to reveal the complete correct sequence. Appendix B.1 adds two successful agent trajectories and one failure.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects the dictionary-subtyping explanation from A ≤ X to X ≤ A, matching the contravariance already expressed in Equation 2. It also explicitly states nondiscriminated-union identities. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: scalable generation of interactive compositional tool-use data, improved downstream performance, and state-of-the-art results on two NESTFUL metrics. Adding 'F1' to the results subsection heading clarifies an already explicit qualification.

C2.justification: New Section 4.5 attributes contrasting transfer results to overfitting and underfitting and suggests an approximately 0.718 validation-accuracy stopping threshold. Section 3.3.3 and Appendix C acknowledge instruction leakage while arguing that it neither substantially harms performance nor makes tasks trivial. These interpretations extend the discussion without changing the main conclusions.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies GRPO training as starting from the base model without preceding SFT, clarifies manual app assignment, and documents which SFT tokens contribute to the loss. Table 6 adds dictionary and multiple-output examples and corrects age-movie's output type to age. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are unchanged. Removing the duplicated WebShop row from Table 1 does not remove a related-work comparison.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds Section 4.5 and acknowledgments, divides Appendix B into GRPO/SFT subsections, inserts the leakage appendix, and makes localized wording corrections and discussion rearrangements.

P2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 2 expand from single-column to full-width displays, with Figure 2 rearranged and the duplicate WebShop row removed. Table 6 is expanded and reordered. Appendix examples gain token highlighting and success/failure markers, and the new leakage examples highlight matching substrings. The overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through the quantified leakage audit, successful and failed GRPO traces, clearer training documentation, and mathematical and presentation corrections. The added GPT-3.5 comparison modestly strengthens evaluation. These gains are limited: principal benchmark results remain unchanged, and neither the proposed 0.718 stopping threshold nor reassurance about leakage is validated through controlled experiments.
